description: The hand-verified expected result for the negative Opengrep SARIF fixture whose originalUriBaseIds entries reference each other in a cycle. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/ -- resolve_uri_base and resolve_sarif_location in paths.py, the classification order in adapters/sarif.py, FIELDS in emit.py and count_records in reconcile.py -- never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match. Key names follow expected/reject-sarif-unresolvable-path.rows.json, the template for every negative expected file in this folder, so one generic loader reads all of them; the blocks this condition needs and that one does not -- termination, guard, conditionality and distinguished_from -- are additive and sit outside rows, rejections, counts and counters, which a loader reads unchanged.

fixture.derivation: A negative fixture is derived from the captured one rather than being an excerpt of it, so the provenance is stated as a derivation. Two of the three results are unmodified captured output: /runs/0/results/0 is deep-equal to harness/artifacts/raw/opengrep.sarif results[0] and to the positive fixture's results[0], and /runs/0/results/2 is deep-equal to that artifact's results[432] and the positive fixture's results[1] -- uriBaseId '%SRCROOT%' included, since the engine stamps it on every result. Two things were added: the run gained an originalUriBaseIds object, which the captured artifact does not emit at all, and a third result, /runs/0/results/1, was synthesized as the defective record.
fixture.captured_provenance: The synthesized record appears in neither harness/artifacts/raw/opengrep.sarif nor oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/opengrep.sarif: searched by (ruleId, uri, startLine) and by uri substring across all 1322 captured results, which carry no finding for OneForOneBlockPusher.java at all. It borrows the ruleId and message of the hardcoded-conditional rule and names a real location -- its region.snippet matches lines 131 to 137 of that file in the pinned tree byte for byte -- so the record is well-formed in every respect except the uriBaseId it points at. That is deliberate: a record defective in two ways would not tell a reader which guard rejected it. The recorded sha256 above is what makes a later edit to the fixture visible: these values are re-derived when the fixture changes, never adjusted to keep a test green.
fixture.not_records: The run carries exactly three members -- originalUriBaseIds, results and tool -- and no invocations block, so unlike the unresolvable-path sibling there are no toolExecutionNotifications here and nothing else in the document is finding-shaped. The five originalUriBaseIds entries are base declarations, not records: counting one would put the raw count at eight and fail the reconciliation identity for a reason that has nothing to do with the adapter.

cycle_verification.checked_against: the fixture itself, re-read after this file was written
cycle_verification.edges: BASE_A -> BASE_B -> BASE_C -> BASE_A, from the uriBaseId member of each entry
cycle_verification.no_cycle_member_terminates_on_an_absolut: BASE_A carries uri 'a/', BASE_B 'b/' and BASE_C 'c/'. All three are relative references and none is a file: URI or an absolute path, so no member of the cycle supplies an absolute ancestor and following the edges can never leave the loop. The absolute base the fixture does carry, PROJECTROOT's file:///opt/, is reachable only from %SRCROOT% and is not a member of the cycle.
cycle_verification.why_three_nodes_and_not_two: A two-node loop A -> B -> A would also be a cycle, but it would fire a defective guard that merely compares each identifier with the one immediately before it. Three nodes make consecutive identifiers always differ -- A then B, B then C, C then A -- so only a guard holding every identifier it has visited can detect the repeat. That is what this fixture exists to separate.
cycle_verification.consequence_if_either_check_were_untrue: The diagnosis recorded in this file would be wrong and the fixture would have to be fixed rather than this file adjusted. A referenced identifier missing from the map would make the rejection attributable to a dangling reference -- what reject-sarif-uribaseid-missing-base.sarif covers -- and fewer than three distinct nodes would let a preceding-identifier comparison pass for a visited set.

routing.detected_by: normalize.shape.is_sarif -- a version of "2.1.0" together with a runs array; those two together are the whole test
routing.routing_decision: normalize.shape.route("opengrep", doc) returns tool "opengrep", shape "sarif", adapter "sarif", scanner_class "sast"
routing.not_a_shape_failure: No normalize.shape.UnknownArtifactShape is expected here. The enclosing document is valid SARIF 2.1.0 -- a malformed base map is not a malformed envelope -- and it routes cleanly; exactly one record inside it is defective, and the adapter rejects that record while still emitting the others. The fixtures that own shape-detection failure are near-sarif-version-only.json, near-sarif-runs-only.json and unknown-shape.json.
routing.negative_routing_test: The mandated negative routing assertion -- that a native artifact must not route to the SARIF adapter -- belongs to test_shape_routing_negative.py and does not use this fixture.

termination.primary_assertion: That the walk terminated at all. This is the assertion this fixture exists for, and it is stated first because it changes what the test is checking: every other negative fixture in this tree fails loudly if the adapter is wrong, while an unguarded walk over this one produces no answer rather than a wrong one. The test does not compare a value against an expectation until it has a value at all.
termination.unusual_failure_mode: A walk with no visited-identifier set and no depth bound follows BASE_A -> BASE_B -> BASE_C -> BASE_A -> BASE_B -> ... forever. Nothing in the cycle is absolute, so there is no exit condition to reach. The normalizer does not raise, does not emit a wrong path and does not produce a partial dataset: it hangs, on one record, and AAP 0.8.1 imposes no time limit anywhere, so nothing interrupts it. A hang produces no dataset at all -- which is why a test asserting only the rejection class would still be the wrong test, and why timing out is a failure rather than an inconclusive result.
termination.walk_outcome_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the BASE_OUTCOME_CYCLE constant -- a literal member of paths.BASE_OUTCOMES, the closed set of seven. Asserted against the module rather than by eye.
termination.walk_detail: the uriBaseId chain revisits 'BASE_A' after BASE_A -> BASE_B -> BASE_C
termination.how_a_test_should_bound_itself: Call the adapter under a timeout and treat expiry as a failure attributable to this condition. A run that returns -- with any result -- has already established the property; the class and counts below then establish that it returned the right one.

guard.which_guard_this_file_asserts: the visited-identifier set, and only that one
guard.depth_bound_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, SARIF_BASE_CHAIN_MAX_DEPTH = 8, the max_depth default of resolve_uri_base
guard.why_the_depth_bound_is_not_reached: The visited set fires on the fourth visit, when the walk returns to BASE_A with a chain of three, well inside the bound of eight. The depth check is evaluated on every iteration and never becomes true, so the outcome is 'cycle' rather than 'over-depth'.
guard.what_a_missing_visited_set_would_produce: Not a hang, given that paths.py also carries the depth bound: the walk would keep going round the loop and stop at a chain of eight with outcome 'over-depth'. The record would still be rejected, still under unresolvable_path, and still with count 1 -- so a test asserting only the class and the counts would pass against a walk that had lost its cycle guard. The outcome name and the chain are what make the difference visible, which is why both are stated here and both belong in the assertion.
guard.what_a_preceding_identifier_comparison_w: The same 'over-depth' misclassification. A guard comparing each identifier only with the one immediately before it never fires on this fixture, because consecutive identifiers always differ. Three nodes are the minimum that separates a genuine visited set from that comparison, and separating them is this fixture's job.
guard.what_neither_guard_would_produce: The hang described under termination. Both guards absent, and the walk has no exit.

conditionality.what_is_unconditional: The termination and its classification. The visited set is internal to resolve_uri_base: it fires on this map regardless of the root, the tool, the runner metadata or anything else a caller supplies, so 'the walk terminates with outcome cycle after BASE_A -> BASE_B -> BASE_C' is a single unconditional expectation and is the primary assertion above.
conditionality.what_the_disposition_depends_on: Whether the terminated record becomes a rejection or a row. AAP 0.5.4 states it directly: a base identifier absent from originalUriBaseIds, or a chain that cycles or exceeds the depth, "resolves through the runner-recorded base only where the runner metadata supplies an explicit base for that tool, and is otherwise a rejection under unresolvable_path". paths.py implements exactly that: BASE_OUTCOME_CYCLE is a member of paths.BASE_OUTCOMES_ELIGIBLE_FOR_METADATA_FALLBACK, and resolve_sarif_location rejects a fallback-eligible outcome only where ToolPathBase.has_explicit_base is false.
conditionality.context_this_file_states_its_expectation: The no-explicit-base context, named in full under resolution_context.tool_path_base. That is the context in which this fixture is a reject- fixture: expected/reject-sarif-unresolvable-path.rows.json assigns "the metadata-backed fallback being refused where no explicit base is recorded" to the five reject-sarif-uribaseid-* fixtures, and AAP 0.9.4 requires a negative fixture and assertion for every rejection condition an exercised adapter can produce. One context, one outcome: there is no branch table in rows, rejections, counts or counters.

alternate_context.label: NOT this file's expectation -- recorded so a reader who drives the fixture differently can see immediately why the numbers differ, rather than concluding the adapter regressed
alternate_context.context: the same fixture under the path base harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json actually records for opengrep: path_base.kind 'scan_root', value '/opt/spark-src', so has_explicit_base is true
alternate_context.outcome: the cycle still terminates identically, and the terminated record then resolves through the runner-recorded base instead of being rejected: three rows, no rejection, parse status clean, and the third row's path_basis is sarif-degenerate-base-metadata-fallback with the walk's cycle detail carried in its corroboration
alternate_context.why_it_is_not_the_expectation_here: It exercises the fallback rather than its refusal, and the fallback's live path is already covered by the positive fixtures: all three SARIF producers in this provisioning record kind 'scan_root' with an explicit value, so opengrep.rows.json and semgrep.rows.json own that route. A fixture named reject- that produced no rejection would leave AAP 0.9.4's per-condition assertion unmet.

conditionality.divergence_recorded: The agent prompt for this file describes the cycle outcome as not conditional on runner metadata, and its dangling-base and relative-ancestor siblings as conditional. Measured against paths.py and AAP 0.5.4 the roles are the other way round: cycle, absent (the dangling base) and over-depth are the three fallback-eligible outcomes and are therefore metadata-conditional, while no-absolute-ancestor and invalid-uri are rejected outright and are unconditional. Recorded rather than quietly resolved, since a reader comparing this file with reject-sarif-uribaseid-relative-no-absolute-ancestor.rows.json will meet the same distinction from the other side. What survives of the prompt's point, and what this file asserts as unconditional, is the termination.

distinguished_from.reject-sarif-uribaseid-missing-base.sari: That fixture's defective record names %REPOSITORYROOT%, which has no entry in the map at all: the walk stops on the first iteration with outcome 'absent' and a chain of one. Here every referenced identifier IS present -- verified entry by entry under fixture.cycle_verification -- so nothing is dangling and the rejection is attributable to the cycle alone. The two are not interchangeable: swap them and the outcome name, the chain length and the detail all change while the class and the count stay the same.
distinguished_from.reject-sarif-uribaseid-overdepth.sarif: That fixture chains forty distinct identifiers, BASE_01 through BASE_40, ending on an absolute file:///opt/spark-src/. Because every identifier is distinct the visited set can never fire there, and only the depth bound stops the walk -- outcome 'over-depth' at a chain of eight, with the remaining thirty-two entries never read. This fixture is the mirror image: the visited set fires at three and the depth bound is never reached. The two exercise different guards and must not be conflated; conflating them would leave one guard untested while both tests passed.
distinguished_from.reject-sarif-uribaseid-relative-no-absol: There the chain SRCROOT -> PROJECTROOT terminates cleanly on an entry that carries no further uriBaseId, and the defect is that the entry it terminates on is relative ('project/'), so no absolute ancestor exists. Outcome 'no-absolute-ancestor', which is not fallback-eligible, so that record is rejected whatever the runner metadata records. Termination there is never in question.
distinguished_from.reject-sarif-uribaseid-invalid-uri.sarif: There an entry's own uri is syntactically invalid ('file://[not-a-valid-host/'), so the walk returns outcome 'invalid-uri' and resolve_sarif_location rejects the record under invalid_uri rather than unresolvable_path. A different class, not merely a different detail.
distinguished_from.reject-sarif-unresolvable-path.sarif: That fixture's defective record shares this one's class, unresolvable_path, and nothing else: its uri is 'urn:example:no-such-coordinate', a foreign scheme classified before any base is resolved, so its walk never runs. Sharing a class is exactly why the detail is quoted in both files -- the class alone cannot tell a cycling chain from a coordinate that names nothing.

chaining_is_legal.statement: A cycle is possible here only because chaining is legal. An originalUriBaseIds entry may itself carry a uriBaseId, and SARIF 2.1.0's own section 3.14.14 example does exactly that, expressing SRCROOT relative to PROJECTROOT. A consumer that read one level would be wrong on conformant input, so the walk must follow the chain -- and once it follows a chain, a malformed map can close a loop.
chaining_is_legal.specification: https://docs.oasis-open.org/sarif/sarif/v2.1.0/sarif-v2.1.0.html section 3.14.14, with the normative consumer procedure at section 3.4.4
chaining_is_legal.the_fixture_uses_both_readings: The same map carries a legitimate two-level chain, %SRCROOT% -> PROJECTROOT resolving to an absolute base, and an illegitimate three-node loop. Two of the three records resolve through the legal chain and one terminates on the loop, so the fixture demonstrates that the guard bounds the walk without disabling the chaining the specification requires. A fixture whose every chain was malformed could not show that.
chaining_is_legal.not_a_producer_defect_this_run_observed: No artifact in harness/artifacts/raw/ emits originalUriBaseIds at all -- opengrep and semgrep emit uriBaseId '%SRCROOT%' with the map absent, and datadog-static-analyzer emits no uriBaseId -- so this map is constructed, not captured. The guard is required by the specification's own chaining rule rather than by anything this provisioning produced, which is why the fixture exists whether or not this run's artifacts contain the case.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent -- exactly emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations.

resolution_context.root: the recorded scan root -- paths.metadata_scan_root(harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json), the document's spark_src member, /opt/spark-src
resolution_context.root_dependence: This fixture is deliberately root-DEPENDENT, unlike its unresolvable-path sibling whose uris are root-relative and whose base is the root itself. Here the surviving uris resolve through the chain onto PROJECTROOT's file:///opt/ joined with %SRCROOT%'s 'spark-src/', which is the absolute directory /opt/spark-src; relativizing back against that same root returns each uri unchanged. Stated because it is a sensitivity, not a detail: under a different root the two surviving rows would come out carrying ../ segments with path_kind outside_root and in_scope false, and the right conclusion would be that the expectation was evaluated against the wrong root -- not that the fixture's base needs editing.
resolution_context.no_absolute_path_is_emitted: The root and the chain's absolute base are named in this prose because a reader cannot check the arithmetic without them. No row's path field carries an absolute value, and emit.py raises on one; the assertion holds for every row below.

tool_path_base.kind_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, PATH_BASE_KIND_NONE -- a literal member of paths.PATH_BASE_KINDS, the vocabulary runner-metadata.json declares. ToolPathBase quotes the document's own instruction for this member: paths.py must reject such a record under unresolvable_path rather than fall back.
tool_path_base.construction: paths.ToolPathBase(tool="opengrep", kind=paths.PATH_BASE_KIND_NONE, base_value=None, scan_root=paths.metadata_scan_root(metadata)) -- the ToolPathBase the test hands to sarif.adapt as tool_base, alongside root=paths.metadata_scan_root(metadata)
tool_path_base.why_constructed_rather_than_read: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json records path_base.kind 'scan_root' with an explicit '/opt/spark-src' for all three SARIF producers, so no recorded entry produces the refusal this fixture is named for. The kind is therefore constructed from the declared vocabulary rather than read from the document, and conditionality.alternate_context records what the recorded entry produces instead. Nothing else about the call is synthetic: the root, the allowlist and the document are the real ones.
tool_path_base.second_net: Even if the has_explicit_base gate were passed, ToolPathBase.base_for_relative() returns None for this kind, and resolve_sarif_location rejects that under unresolvable_path too -- with a different detail naming the kind that supplies no single directory. The gate is what fires here; the second branch is why no reading of this kind resolves.

uri_base_id_walk_outcomes.%SRCROOT%: resolved -- chain %SRCROOT% -> PROJECTROOT, base /opt/spark-src, detail "resolved through %SRCROOT% -> PROJECTROOT to '/opt/spark-src'"
uri_base_id_walk_outcomes.BASE_A: cycle -- chain BASE_A -> BASE_B -> BASE_C, no base

resolution_context.path_basis_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, BASIS_SARIF_BASE_CHAIN. Note that this is NOT the basis the positive opengrep fixture records: there the map is absent, the walk reports 'absent' and the rows resolve through the metadata fallback under BASIS_SARIF_METADATA_BASE. Here the specification's own procedure completes, so the surviving rows are the one case in this tree where a SARIF path is established by the section 3.4.4 route rather than by the documented fallback.
resolution_context.severity_source: No surviving result states a level, and neither rule carries properties.severity or properties.problem.severity, so each severity_native is the level its own rule states under defaultConfiguration.level and each severity_norm comes from the SARIF level table: error High, warning Medium, note Low, none Info.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on every row. A SARIF result names a code location rather than a package, and this shape supplies no coordinate to carry.
resolution_context.no_secret_value: Nothing in this fixture is a credential, a token or a matched secret, and no field below carries one. The only fields with free text are message and rule_id, both taken verbatim from the rule's own description. This file is committed to git.

rejection_boundary.statement: A base chain that cannot be resolved leaves the record with no path at all, and that is a rejection. A path that resolves somewhere unwanted is a kept row with in_scope false. The defective record here resolves to nothing: its only route to a path was the base chain, and the chain closes on itself.
rejection_boundary.why_it_can_only_be_a_rejection: path is one of only two never-absent fields in the twelve-field schema, the other being severity_norm: emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS carries path, and emit.OPTIONAL_FIELDS is exactly severity_native, start_line, cwe, cve and package_coordinate. A record with no resolvable path therefore has no valid row representation at all -- emit.py raises on a null path rather than writing one -- so counting it under a named class is the only outcome that neither drops the record nor invents a coordinate for it.
rejection_boundary.the_uri_alone_would_have_resolved: Read on its own the defective record's uri is a perfectly ordinary root-relative path to a real in-scope file, and it is the same file the missing-base and relative-ancestor fixtures use for their defective records. That is the point of the fixture: the record is rejected for the base it points at, not for the path it names, and no fixture in this tree rejects a record for both at once.
rejection_boundary.no_guessed_path: The rejected record is rejected and counted, never given a path. Nothing in this file supplies a coordinate for it, not even the obvious one its uri would have produced under a resolvable base -- writing that down would assert the opposite of what this fixture exists to assert.

not_a_rejection.case: a path resolving outside the twelve authoritative globs
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted under rows_out_of_scope

not_a_rejection.case: an archive member, or a container outside the root
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted in non_filesystem_paths and serialized <container-relative-to-root>!<member> with ../ segments preserved

not_a_rejection.case: a path in a src/test tree
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false; the exclusion is literal and removes the path from scope rather than from the dataset

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of runs[].results[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction
counts.raw_count_authority: normalize.reconcile.count_records("opengrep", doc), whose SARIF traversal sums the length of each run's results array and builds no row, resolves no path and maps no severity. It is the independent half of the identity: a count taken from the traversal that builds the rows would satisfy the assertion while testing nothing. It reads no originalUriBaseIds and walks no chain, so this fixture's defect cannot reach it -- which is what keeps the left-hand side of the identity fixed at 3 whatever the walk does.
counts.rejections_by_class_note: One class, one record. The other nine members of paths.REJECT_CLASSES are absent from this fixture, and a per-class reading that reported them as zero rather than as absent would be equally correct here; what matters is that the single entry names unresolvable_path exactly.

four_reported_counters.authority: AAP 0.5.4 -- the four counts reported per tool
four_reported_counters.note: Named here rather than restated with their values. The counters block below is the single measurement, and a number carried twice inside one document is a number that can drift; counters_note gives the reason each of the four is zero.

counts.parse_status_authority: harness/lib/normalize/cli.py, PARSE_STATUS_PARTIAL = "partial", assigned as partial where there are rejections and clean where there are none. Partial is right precisely because the adapter did not abandon the artifact: every parsable record was emitted and the one rejected record is counted under its class, with its parser reason retained. This is deliberately not normalize.reconcile's STATUS_PASS / STATUS_FAIL / STATUS_NOT_APPLICABLE vocabulary, which describes an assertion's outcome rather than an artifact's parse.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): twenty authored keys, one path_kind_* per member of paths.PATH_KINDS and one severity_basis_* per member of severity.BASIS_VALUES, twenty-nine in total.
counters_note: Three things a reader must not "correct". First, rule_id_from_rule_id is 3 while the severity and path counters are 2: the rule step is step 2 of the classification order and the path step is step 4, so the rejected record resolves its rule identifier before it is rejected, and it never reaches severity or a path kind. That asymmetry is the classification order made visible, not a miscount. Second, no counter records the walk: there is no counter for a base chain, a cycle or a fallback, so the cycle is visible only in the rejection's outcome and detail -- which is why those are asserted rather than inferred from a count. Third, the four counters AAP 0.5.4 has reported per tool are all 0 here: every result carries exactly one location, so multi_location_records is 0; the one rule that names a weakness names exactly one, so multi_valued_cwe_records is 0; no rule string carries a CVE identifier, so multi_valued_cve_records is 0; and both emitted paths name a file inside the scanned tree, so non_filesystem_paths is 0.

rows.message: This if statement will always have the same behavior and is therefore unnecessary.

User data flows into this manually-constructed SQL string. User data can be safely inserted into SQL strings using prepared statements or an object-relational mapper (ORM). Manually-constructed SQL strings is a possible indicator of SQL injection, which could let an attacker steal or manipulate data from the database. Instead, use prepared statements (`connection.PreparedStatement`) or a safe library.

row_derivations.rule_id_source: the result's own ruleId; no ruleIndex and no rule reference is present
row_derivations.severity_native_note: the result states no level of its own, so the level is the one its rule states -- SARIF 2.1.0's own derivation, not an inference
row_derivations.path_derivation: uriBaseId %SRCROOT% walks to PROJECTROOT, whose uri file:///opt/ is absolute, so the chain resolves to /opt/spark-src with %SRCROOT%'s own 'spark-src/' joined beneath it. The uri is then joined onto that base and relativized against the same root, which returns it unchanged. Two levels, which is why reading one would be wrong.
row_derivations.cwe_absent_reason: the rule carries no properties.cwe and its properties.tags array is empty, so no CWE token exists to collect
row_derivations.anchor_note: The first surviving row, and the one whose result immediately precedes the defective record. It establishes that the adapter reached the defective record having already emitted a row, so a suite that saw one row could not mistake a hang for a rejection.

row_derivations.rule_id_source: the result's own ruleId; no ruleIndex and no rule reference is present
row_derivations.severity_native_note: the result states no level of its own, so the level is the one its rule states -- SARIF 2.1.0's own derivation, not an inference
row_derivations.path_derivation: the same two-level chain as row 0, resolved once per record rather than cached; %SRCROOT% -> PROJECTROOT -> /opt/spark-src, joined and relativized back to the root unchanged

cwe_source.text: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

row_derivations.cve_absent_reason: no string on the result or its rule matches CVE-<4-digit year>-<4-or-more digits>; the rule's remaining tags are MEDIUM CONFIDENCE, two OWASP category labels and security, none of which is a CVE identifier
row_derivations.anchor_note: The second surviving row, after the rejection and from a different module and rule, so the fixture proves the adapter carried on past the rejected record rather than stopping at it. Line 72 of the pinned DiskStore.scala is the interpolated string argument of the SparkException.internalError(...) call that opens on line 71, and the file is 380 lines, so start_line is within the file.

rejections.locator_note: The pointer and the run_index / result_index pair name the same record. The pair is carried as well because normalize.adapters.sarif passes exactly run_index, result_index and rule_id into the rejection it builds, so a produced Rejection's record_identity and this expectation can be compared directly, without translating one coordinate system into the other.
rejections.reject_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_UNRESOLVABLE_PATH constant -- a literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, the closed set of ten. Written verbatim rather than paraphrased, and asserted against the module rather than by eye: a test that only counts rejections cannot tell one condition from another, so the class name is what carries the assertion. The module's own comment names this class as the destination AAP 0.5.4 routes the base-absent, cycle, over-depth, degenerate-base and no-absolute-ancestor cases to, with the sub-reason in the detail rather than in a separate class.
rejections.classification_step: step 4 of the adapter's fixed classification order -- shape, rule identifier, message, path, start_line. Steps 1 to 3 all pass on this record: it is a JSON object, it carries a valid ruleId that resolves to /runs/0/tool/driver/rules/0, and it carries a non-empty message.text. That is deliberate, so the only thing left to reject it for is its path.
rejections.start_line_never_examined: Step 5 is never reached, so this record's region.startLine of 131 is never examined and non_integer_start_line is not in play. Worth stating because the fixture does give the defective record a startLine, and a reader could otherwise expect an interaction between the two conditions.
rejections.uri_form_authority: paths.parse_uri_reference classifies it as URI_FORM_RELATIVE with no leading slash, so it is neither invalid_uri, nor a foreign scheme, nor an archive reference, nor filesystem-absolute. A relative reference carrying a uriBaseId is exactly the input the section 3.4.4 walk exists for, which is why this record reaches the walk where reject-sarif-unresolvable-path.sarif's does not.
rejections.fallback_refused_because: the stated tool_path_base carries kind 'none' with no base value, so ToolPathBase.has_explicit_base is false and resolve_sarif_location takes the refusal branch. AAP 0.5.4: the documented degenerate-base fallback "is not a catch-all -- it applies where the metadata makes the base known, and everywhere else the record is rejected and counted rather than guessed."
rejections.expected_detail: the uriBaseId chain revisits 'BASE_A' after BASE_A -> BASE_B -> BASE_C; and the runner metadata records path_base.kind 'none' with no explicit base for 'opengrep', so the documented degenerate-base fallback does not apply and this record is rejected rather than resolved through a guess
rejections.expected_detail_note: The detail is the sub-reason AAP 0.5.4 requires a rejection to carry, and it is quoted in full because every rejection class in this pipeline covers several routes: naming unresolvable_path alone would not distinguish this record from a foreign-scheme uri, a dangling base or an over-deep chain. A test may assert the class exactly and the detail by its distinguishing substrings -- "revisits 'BASE_A'", the chain "BASE_A -> BASE_B -> BASE_C" and "no explicit base" -- rather than by full-string equality, since the detail is prose composed from the walk's own report and the recorded kind.
rejections.record_identity_note: The adapter supplies run_index, result_index and rule_id; the resolver adds the raw uri and, where one is present as a non-empty string, the raw uriBaseId. Enough to find the record in the artifact again, and never the record itself and never a secret value. The uriBaseId is the field that makes this rejection diagnosable at all -- without it, the identity would name a record whose uri looks perfectly resolvable.
rejections.why_not_a_row: There is no path to put in the row. path is never absent from a row, so a record whose only route to a coordinate is a base chain that closes on itself has no valid row representation, and the alternatives -- dropping it, or joining its uri onto a guessed base -- would each hide it. Counting it under a named class keeps it visible and keeps the arithmetic honest.
rejections.contributes_no_severity_literal: The rejected record is never fed to the severity tally, so no native literal from it reaches severity-map.md. That document reports literals against the rows the dataset contains, and this record contributes none -- which is also why severity_from_rule_default_configuration is 2 rather than 3 while rule_id_from_rule_id is 3.
rejections.contributes_no_counter: It increments no path_kind_* and no severity_basis_* counter, and it is not counted in rows_in_scope or rows_out_of_scope. in_scope is a property of a row, and this record has none; the file its uri names is inside the twelve globs, which is deliberately not recorded as a scope decision here because no row exists to carry one.

corroboration.note: The two surviving results are two of the captured results the positive sibling covers -- this file's row 0 is that file's row for FileSegmentManagedBuffer.java and its row 1 is that file's row for DiskStore.scala -- and all twenty-four field comparisons agree. What deliberately does NOT agree is the path_basis: there the map is absent and both rows resolve through the metadata fallback, here the map is present and both resolve through the section 3.4.4 chain. Twelve identical field values from two different resolution routes is the invariant the path work exists for -- a row's path means the same thing regardless of which route established it. Recorded after the fact rather than as the source of these values: each value here was derived from the fixture and the authored contracts, so a future disagreement between this file and the adapter is a finding to diagnose rather than a diff to apply. The defective record has no counterpart to corroborate against: it is this fixture's own synthesized addition and it contributes no dataset row.
corroboration.not_corroborated_by_a_run: No number in this file was taken from a normalizer or adapter invocation. The independent check available to a reader is arithmetic and textual: three results in the fixture, two rows listed, one rejection listed, and every field traced to a JSON pointer that can be read out of the fixture by hand.
